newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom sees cable profit by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom sees cable profit by 2000.

text.p: German telecommunications firm Deutsche Telekom AG plans to bring its cable business into the black by raising prices and moving into the commercial television market, German weekly Der Spiegel said in its weekend edition.
The magazine also said Deutsche Telekom's cable business, which has for years posted losses, recorded a 500 million mark loss last year.
A Telekom spokesperson declined to comment on the figure.

Spiegel said Telekom chairman Ron Sommer was aiming to swing the cable business to profit by the turn of the century, not by 2007 as the firm had previously predicted, and would do this partly via higher prices.

Television providers, who until now were able to broadcast to homes "virtually for nothing", according to Sommer, would have now have to pay more, Spiegel said, since costs had already risen this year from around one million to 3.2 million marks per year.
Spiegel also said private customers could also face higher prices this year -- with rises of around one mark per month being considered.

A spokesperson for Telekom said price changes for programme providers would be made, because Telekom's cable business had to be refinanced and the gap narrowed between the cost of satellite and cable television.
But he added that no decision had been made about price rises for private households.
As well as price changes, Deutsche Telekom is also keen to take a more active role in the commercial television market, Spiegel reported Sommer as saying.
Sommer has plans to sell decoders for digital channel reception, manage television subscriptions and engage in programme marketing, the report said.

Deutsche Telekom is the only firm in Germany which owns and operates a national cable television network, connecting around 17 million homes. Because of competition at the local network level, Telekom has around six million subscribers under direct contract.
Top media executives and state politicians are due to hold round table media discussions with Telekom's Sommer on May 20.

The talks are an attempt to break a deadlock over the expansion of cable television networks and the introduction of widescale digital TV programming, which industry infighting has delayed for almost two years.

Telekom shares hit a new record Friday, reaching an intraday peak of 40 marks -- a gain of almost 10 percent since the shares were offered at 28.50 marks on November 18 last year. The stock ended trade at 39.95 marks, up 3.2 percent.
The company's annual news conference is due on Tuesday.
